topic: Multi-intent task decomposition for LLM tool and skill routing
name: Corpus2Skill — Don't Retrieve, Navigate: Distilling Enterprise Knowledge into Navigable Agent Skills
description: Corpus2Skill / C2S (arXiv:2604.14572; Sun, Wei, Hsieh, 2026) compiles a document corpus OFFLINE into a hierarchical tree of navigable Anthropic Skills, then lets an LLM agent traverse that tree at serve time instead of running retrieval. The compile phase summarizes each document (Claude Haiku 4.5), embeds and iteratively clusters documents into a multi-level hierarchy, and writes routing-oriented LLM summaries (Claude Sonnet 4.6) at each level: root clusters become SKILL.md directories, sub-clusters become INDEX.md group directories, leaf documents go to a separate document store (documents.json), with an entity_index.json and `## Related Skills` cross-references. At serve time an agent walks the tree via file navigation (ls/cat via code execution) and a get_document tool — no vector DB, BM25, or embedding model online. It outperforms dense retrieval, RAPTOR, and agentic RAG on WixQA and a 10-dataset macro-F1. Code: github.com/dukesun99/Corpus2Skill.
decomposition_method: skill-tree traversal (offline corpus compilation, not query decomposition). The compound 'decomposition' is over the CORPUS, performed offline: embed documents, iteratively cluster into a multi-level cluster hierarchy, and generate LLM-written routing summaries at each level. At query time there is no explicit splitting of the prompt into sub-tasks; instead a single navigating agent decomposes the search by walking the pre-built skill tree (progressive disclosure). This is the paper's contrast paradigm: navigation replaces both embedding retrieval and trained routers/classifiers.
decomposition_granularity: semantic unit — clusters of topically related documents. Each tree node (SKILL.md / INDEX.md) is a routing-oriented summary of a document cluster identifying topic area, question types, and key terms; leaves are individual documents fetched by ID.
ordering_strategy: dynamic (mid-traversal re-plan). The agent descends the tree greedily toward promising branches and re-decides at each node based on the summaries it reads; it can backtrack from unproductive paths and cross-jump laterally via `## Related Skills` / entity_index. There is no fixed DAG or parallel fan-out — traversal order is decided online by the agent as it reads decision-point summaries. [uncertain]
decomposition_validation: Offline structural validation rather than per-query solvability checking. Compilation produces routing-oriented summaries so each file functions as a reliable decision point, and the hierarchy is shaped/validated against Anthropic Skills API limits (8 skills/request, 200 files/skill, 30 MB/skill) which cap top-level clusters and tree depth (compact merging when exceeded). There is no AOP-style reward-model check of completeness/non-redundancy of a per-query decomposition; quality is enforced at corpus-compile time and empirically via retrieval/answer metrics. The serve-time agent is instructed to keep at least two candidate skills alive before committing (a soft completeness heuristic). [uncertain]
hierarchy_depth: multi-level tree. Root SKILL.md clusters -> INDEX.md sub-cluster groups -> leaf documents in a document store. With K=10 the paper reports a 3-level hierarchy (6 top-level skills, 665 navigation files). Depth is bounded by the 200-files-per-skill Skills API budget.
router_type: tree traversal. Routing is performed by an LLM agent navigating a static filesystem of skill files (reading SKILL.md/INDEX.md, drilling down, backtracking, lateral cross-jumps), as opposed to a single/multi-label classifier, retrieve-then-rerank, or upfront DAG planner.
routing_model: prompted LLM agent at serve time (Claude family) navigating via file-browsing + get_document tools; compilation-time summarization uses Claude Haiku 4.5 (per-document summary cards) and Claude Sonnet 4.6 (cluster summaries). Clustering uses embeddings (e.g., Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B in the dense baseline) offline. No trained router/classifier and no online embedding similarity — routing is the agent reading human-readable summaries.
handles_ambiguity: multiple-parallel-candidates kept alive plus backtracking. The serve-time system prompt instructs the agent to keep at least two candidate skills alive before committing to a path, to consult entity_index.json when a specific named entity is referenced, and to cross-jump via the `## Related Skills` block when its initial branch proves insufficient. Ambiguity is resolved by exploration/backtracking and cross-branch synthesis rather than asking the user or abstaining. [uncertain]
fallback_behavior: re-navigation / backtracking. If a branch is unproductive the agent abandons it and explores alternative skills (related-skills cross-references, entity index) or other branches; there is no human escalation. If navigation surfaces nothing relevant the agent answers from what it found (the paper notes navigation is not universally better and can underperform flat retrieval on open-domain pools). No explicit abort. [uncertain]
skill_pool_scale_and_retrieval: skill-tree traversal as the scaling mechanism. Instead of embedding top-k or rerank over a large pool, the corpus is pre-organized into a navigable hierarchy whose top level fits the Skills API 8-skill cap; the agent always starts from a compact bird's-eye view (all skill descriptions pre-loaded via progressive disclosure) and drills down, so per-query context holds summaries not the whole corpus. Scaling is bounded by Skills API limits (8 skills/request, 200 files/skill, 30 MB/skill) and compact-merging of deep trees. Input-token cost is high (~53K input tokens/query) because navigation files are reloaded each call, partly mitigated by prompt caching.
router_agent_asymmetry: Low asymmetry — the same single agent both routes (reads summaries) and consumes evidence; there is no separate router model with privileged skill text. The summaries the agent navigates are the same compiled artifacts; the only asymmetry is summary-vs-full-document (the agent sees cluster summaries before fetching full document text by ID). [uncertain]
execution_pattern: ReAct-style sequential navigation loop. A single agent iteratively reads a navigation file, decides the next move (descend, backtrack, lateral cross-jump, or fetch a document), one step at a time, until it has enough evidence to answer — not parallel fan-out or a precomputed DAG.
parallel_vs_concurrent: Sequential (neither parallel nor concurrent). Tree traversal is a one-agent, one-step-at-a-time loop; the paper does not parallelize branch exploration. [uncertain]
dependency_detection: Not applicable in the DAG sense. Ordering is emergent from greedy traversal and backtracking; there is no explicit independence/dependency classification of sub-tasks. Cross-branch synthesis (combining evidence from multiple subgroups) is enabled by related-skills links and the entity index rather than a dependency graph. [uncertain]
result_aggregation: LLM synthesis over gathered documents. The agent combines evidence collected across visited branches/documents (cross-branch synthesis) into a grounded answer; aggregation is the agent re-reading what it retrieved during navigation. [uncertain]
mid_chain_feedback: hard — each navigation step re-plans based on summaries read so far, with explicit backtracking and lateral cross-jumps when a branch proves insufficient; structural visibility of the hierarchy is what enables online re-routing.
benchmark_name: WixQA (enterprise customer-support QA) as the primary benchmark, plus a 10-dataset / 10-subset generalization suite (macro-average F1).
multi_intent_coverage: Partial / implicit. The system targets complex multi-hop support questions and compliance-critical lookups requiring evidence combined across branches (cross-branch synthesis), so multi-hop (dependent/scattered-evidence) intent is covered, but the benchmarks are QA corpora rather than an explicit parallel/sequential multi-intent tool-routing taxonomy (no BFCL-style parallel/multiple categories). [uncertain]
accuracy_metric: Retrieval/answer-quality metrics: Token F1 (0.460, +19% over Agentic 0.388, +27% over Dense 0.363), BERTScore, Factuality (0.729 vs Agentic 0.724, RAPTOR 0.675), Context Recall (0.652 vs RAPTOR 0.616, Agentic 0.481), Context Precision, and Hallucination Rate (lowest among multi-turn methods); plus 10-dataset macro-average F1. Outcome/grounding metrics, not exact-match tool names or process supervision.
clarification_capability: Not measured. There is no when-to-ask vs when-to-answer mechanism; the agent resolves under-specification by exploring/backtracking the tree, not by asking the user. The benchmarks do not test clarification efficiency. [uncertain]
process_vs_outcome_eval: Outcome/grounding-focused (F1, Factuality, Context Recall/Precision, Hallucination Rate on the final answer and retrieved context). Navigation traces are analyzed qualitatively (direct descent vs cross-branch exploration) but there is no quantitative per-step process-reward score. [uncertain]
eval_stability: Reproducible offline setup — fixed corpora compiled into a static skill filesystem, no live external tool/search APIs at serve time, so it avoids the API-drift issues of live-tool benchmarks (though it is not the StableToolBench cached-server design). [uncertain]
integration_pattern: Standalone offline compiler producing a static skill filesystem (output under <output_dir>/.claude/skills/) that is uploaded to Anthropic's Skills API; at serve time an in-context LLM agent uses progressive-disclosure skill discovery plus file-navigation (code execution) and a get_document tool. Compiler-plus-agent service rather than a LangGraph node or inference-engine layer.
routing_layer: Application-layer (agent + Skills API); no inference-engine-layer routing.
latency_overhead: Multi-turn navigation adds round-trips and large input-token cost: navigation files are included in every Skills API call (~53K input tokens/query), giving ~$0.17/query (≈$0.153/query, ~1.9x single-shot retrievers ~$0.007-0.012). Prompt caching reuses ~70% of the prompt across consecutive turns and ~100% across queries hitting the same top-level branch, cutting cost. Offline compilation is a one-time cost. Positioned for high-value queries where answer quality justifies the premium.
online_adaptation: Static at deploy. The skill tree is fixed after offline compilation; there is no bandit/RL or log-driven re-routing online. Recompiling the corpus is the update path. [uncertain]
adoption: Open-source early release (github.com/dukesun99/Corpus2Skill; pipeline works end-to-end, rough edges remain) tied to the 2026 arXiv paper (arXiv:2604.14572). Research + open-source; depends on Anthropic Skills API. Not a separate commercial product.
